newsitem.title: USA: Clinton gets autographed ball at Bulls-Bullets game.
newsitem.headline: Clinton gets autographed ball at Bulls-Bullets game.

text.p: - The No. 1 U.S. basketball fan took in the world's No. 1 basketball attraction on Friday night as President Bill Clinton watched Michael Jordan and the Chicago Bulls defeat the Washington Bullets.

Clinton took home a souvenir as the defending National Basketball Association champion Bulls presented him with an autographed ball in their locker room before the game. The president also visited the Bullets dressing room before tipoff at the U.S. Air Arena.
Accompanied by U.S. Commerce Secretary Bill Daley, a native of Chicago, Clinton sat several rows up from the floor at centre court -- just another fan in the sell-out crowd of 18,756.
During the game he munched on snacks and clapped enthusiastically when players from either team made a nice pass or drained a long basket.

The president did a credible job of remaining neutral, but he did some hard cheering as the Bullets mounted a fourth-quarter charge that was quelled by an eye-popping offensive display by Jordan, who ended the game with 36 points.
